:::caution[On main, next release]
This page was written from `main` at 9d25dc1. These notes are for a release that is not out. HotLoop 4.17.0 is the latest one you can install.
:::

The release where HotLoop stops being one image. IoT, Edge, the Gateway and the
Edge Relay all ship from this tag, in lockstep, each with its own image and its
own chart. On top of that: devices that announce themselves over MQTT, history
written out to the plant's own database, a database you pick (SQLite, Postgres
or TimescaleDB), an Edge that keeps working with the WAN dead, and boxes that
follow `:stable` and roll a bad update back on their own. Coming from 4.17.0 the
Gateway is a plain `helm upgrade`. Read "Upgrading from 4.17.0" below before you
touch a running plant, because a couple of defaults moved.

There is no 4.18.0, 4.18.1 or 4.18.2 you can install. I tagged all three, and
all three release runs died in the Test job before they published a single
image, chart or release. CI runs Docker on a small shared runner and my lab runs
Podman on a big box, and the integration services' script had three things only
the lab forgave. The network-discovery image was built without naming its
Containerfile. InfluxDB 3's token file went in readable by root alone, which
Docker leaves it as and Podman quietly hands to the container's user. SQL
Server died at boot when the runner was busy starting everything else, so it
starts on its own first now and gets tried again if it dies. The port 465 test
had no relay to run against, so it skipped, and a skip fails the release. The
fixes are in the test scripts, with one exception: two reloads of the runtime at
once could race on a worker, and reloads take turns now. This is everything
4.18.0 was going to be.

The full notes are in the README:
What changed in 4.18.3.

## In short

- **Four products, four images, four charts, one tag.** `hotloop-iot` and
  `hotloop-edge` are new on ghcr.io and in the chart repository. The Gateway
  keeps `ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop` and the chart `hotloop`, so nobody running
  it changes anything. A product is a build, not a setting: the OPC UA server
  isn't switched off in the IoT image, it isn't in it. See
  docs/PRODUCTS.md.
- **MQTT discovery.** Point ESPHome, Zigbee2MQTT, Tasmota or a Shelly at the
  broker and it shows up, reading. It can't command anything until an admin
  accepts it and arms each point by hand. Network discovery (mDNS, SSDP, DHCP)
  listens and sends nothing unless you list a network to probe.
- **Historian targets.** Every reading HotLoop keeps also goes to the plant's
  own PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB, SQL Server, InfluxDB or MySQL/MariaDB, the same
  rows with the same quality.
- **The database is a setting.** SQLite, PostgreSQL or TimescaleDB per product,
  from the same binary. A Pi doesn't need a 300 MB database image.
- **Edge keeps the plant running with the WAN dead,** and its store and forward
  queue survives the ugly cases: a boot during an outage, a link that dies
  without a reset, a replay that has to outrun the plant.
- **Every box follows `:stable` and updates itself,** and a release that can't
  start is rolled back. Migrations only add, and an app refuses to start on a
  schema two releases ahead of it, so that rollback is always safe.
- **The Edge Relay** takes a pushed config live, with no restart and no lost
  Sparkplug session, and discovers devices on a broker like the Gateway does.
- **Every image carries every third-party license,** and a GPL module stops the
  build.
- **The sun.** Sunrise, sunset and the sun's height, worked out on the box from
  a latitude and a longitude.

### API changes

- New routes: `/api/discovery`, `/api/network-discovery`, `/api/mqtt/brokers`,
  `/api/broker/logins`, `/api/historian/targets`,
  `GET /api/entities/{entity_id}/image` and `POST /api/fleet/{id}/update`. All
  in docs/API.md.
- `GET /api/status` says `product` and `features`, and the image digest. A route
  for a feature the product you're talking to doesn't have answers `404` with
  the product that does, instead of pretending. Every route is still there in
  every product.
- New permission `fleet.update`, admin only. The operator role didn't change.

### Upgrading from 4.17.0

- `helm upgrade <release> hotloop/hotloop --version 4.18.3
  --reset-then-reuse-values`. I rendered the 4.17.0 and 4.18.3 Gateway charts
  side by side: the same eight objects, the same selectors, the same volume
  claims. Plain `--reuse-values` renders too this time, but it replays 4.17.0's
  values and drops every new default, so use the reset form or your values file.
- Migrations 0016 to 0022 run on start (MQTT discovery, broker logins, MQTT
  sources, historian targets, network finds, and two more for what the MQTT sources speak).
  All additive. `pg_dump` first, like always.
- **`edgePublish.queueMaxBytes` defaults to 64 MiB now, not unbounded.** Past
  it the oldest readings are dropped and counted. An unbounded queue filled the
  volume in a long outage, which is worse, but it is a changed default: size it
  from your own reading rate (about 180 bytes a reading) or set it to `0` to
  keep the old behavior. An upgrade with `--reuse-values` keeps whatever you
  had.
- **Broker logins.** Logins you make in Settings, MQTT carry topic rules from a
  profile. Logins from `HOTLOOP_BROKER_USERS` are untouched and can do anything,
  exactly as before. A broker with no `HOTLOOP_BROKER_USERS` starts now, and only
  HotLoop and the logins made in it get in.
- **Going back to 4.17.0** works: the schema only grew, and 4.17.0 runs on it.
  `test/prevrelease.sh` proves that against the published 4.17.0 image before
  every release. From here on the app also counts how far ahead its database is
  and refuses by name at two releases, so a rollback is never a surprise.
- **Edge Relay:** upgrade it with `--reset-then-reuse-values` too. Quadlet users
  take the new `edge-relay.container`, which follows `:stable` instead of
  pinning 4.17.0, and the healthcheck that makes a bad update roll back.
- **Quadlet units for IoT, Edge and the Gateway are new.** 4.17.0 only had the
  relay's. They are under `deploy/quadlet/`, one directory per product.

### What isn't proven

- **Edge and IoT as live Quadlet units under systemd,** except IoT's SQLite
  unit, which was run. The rest are generated from the Gateway's, checked
  against them, and not started. The Gateway's units were run for real,
  rootless under systemd, including an update that migrates and then can't
  start and gets rolled back. A real Pi under systemd as root: not yet.
- **Moving a site up a product as a `helm upgrade` on a real cluster,** and going
  back down one. The Quadlet move, IoT to Edge to Gateway on one database
  volume, has been run.
- **Discovery against real devices is proven against recordings** of real
  installs, not against devices on a bench here. ESPHome's `mqtt:` component
  doesn't build for a host, so there is no live ESPHome in CI.
- **The 32-bit arm images on real hardware.** A Pi 3 under load: not yet.
